title.narrative: Supporting Public Sector Management Reform Program, Subprogram 1

description.narrative: The proposed program supports Tuvalu's efforts to strengthen fiscal and climate resilience, and will support (i) public financial management (PFM) to achieve fiscal sustainability; (ii) the performance, transparency, and accountability of Tuvalu's public enterprises to strengthen fiscal resilience; and (iii) the country's energy transition and climate resilience through improved PFM and commitments undertaken in accordance with its nationally determined contribution goal of achieving 100% reliance on renewable energy by 2030.

description.narrative: Policy Action/s as listed by the project staff.

Reform area: Fiscal and public resource management strengthened
Outcome: At least two government contracts incorporate sustainable considerations, and one procurement framework agreement put in place
Description: To enhance fiscal discipline and optimize public resource spending: (i) the Secretary to the Government's Office issued a circular (a) directing all government agencies to submit mandatory procurement plans and adhere to a centralized approval process, and (b) imposing strict disciplinary measures for noncompliance, to improve observance of procurement regulation that ensures value for money in procuring of public goods and services; and (ii) the Cabinet approved the design and implementation of the full e-Government Procurement (eGP) system (concept note), which aims at streamlining the public procurement process by reducing paperwork and lowering costs through reduced administrative expenses.

Reform area: Fiscal and public resource management strengthened
Outcome: At least two government contracts incorporate sustainable considerations, and one procurement framework agreement put in place
Description: To ensure sustainable revenue generation from fishing licenses and collections through effective conservation, management and sustainable use of the county's marine resources: (i) the Fisheries Management Act 2025 was enacted to strengthen legal and institutional framework that, among others, fosters sustainability and predictability of revenues from fisheries licenses; and (ii) (a) the Ministry of Natural Resources and Development issued an order to establish a new Fisheries Authority to strengthen accountability and enforcement in the fisheries sector to protect national income, (b) the Fisheries Authority confirmed the appointment of its board of directors represented with at least one-woman director, and (c) the Cabinet approved the appointment of 3 independent board members to ensure the Authority's effective functioning.

Reform area: Fiscal and public resource management strengthened
Outcome: At least two government contracts incorporate sustainable considerations, and one procurement framework agreement put in place
Description: To further strengthen fisheries management, and ensure the Fisheries Authority functions effectively and delivers measurable results, the Board of Directors of the Authority will: (i) endorse corporate plan for the Authority that includes clearly defined set of performance measures, a comprehensive risk management plan, a medium-term strategic framework with resource allocation, and a robust monitoring and evaluation system; and (ii) approve the allocation of A$2 million in the FY2027 national budget, which will include financing of a program to improve the economic opportunities for women in fisheries sector.

Reform area: Fiscal and public resource management strengthened
Outcome: At least two government contracts incorporate sustainable considerations, and one procurement framework agreement put in place
Description: To further strengthen the procurement systems and practices: (i) the Cabinet will approve amendments to the Public Procurement Regulations (amended in 2021), which incorporates the following key features: enhanced use of the eGP system, promotion of sustainable procurement practices, with a focus on local participation, gender and circular economy considerations, and operations and maintenance; strengthened evaluation methodologies to achieve value for money; expanded use of framework agreements; adoption of standardized procurement templates; improved compliance with the Annual Procurement Plan; (ii) MFED will approve the amendments to the Procurement Manual to ensure alignment with the revised regulations and to support their effective implementation; and (iii) The MFED will approve the eGP framework including eGP policy, technical requirements, procurement options and implementation roadmap to operationalize the system.

Reform area: Fiscal and public resource management strengthened
Outcome: At least two government contracts incorporate sustainable considerations, and one procurement framework agreement put in place
Description: To implement the Strategic Plan for TOMRS the Cabinet will: (i) approve cost sharing policy to improve public financial sustainability, enhance efficient resource allocation and reduce overuse and abuse of the referral scheme; and (ii) adopt clear referral criteria for better selection of referral applications, optimization of medical expenditures and tracking of referral patterns and provisions to address the needs of women headed and vulnerable households.

Reform area: Fiscal and public resource management strengthened
Outcome: At least two government contracts incorporate sustainable considerations, and one procurement framework agreement put in place
Description: To optimize the use of scarce government financial resources, better manage the financial implications on central government budget, and ensure citizens receive timely and quality medical care, the Cabinet considered the review of the Tuvalu Overseas Medical Referral Scheme (TOMRS) and approved the related Strategy, which: (i) is gender inclusive; (ii) streamlines administrative processes to achieve cost savings; (iii) optimizes the utilization of medical resources; and (iv) strengthens the analytical capacity to facilitate more effective and gender responsive resource allocation.

Reform area: Fiscal and public resource management strengthened
Outcome: At least two government contracts incorporate sustainable considerations, and one procurement framework agreement put in place
Description: To strengthen PFM practices, the government through MFED will implement the PFM Road Map priorities, which will (i) develop and publish Citizen's Budget to strengthen public trust in government through clear and effective communication of the public finance information; and (ii) resume and complete the reconciliation of government's bank accounts that has been inactive since 2020 to be reviewed and confirmed by the Auditor General to ensure accuracy in financial reporting, strengthen compliance and accountability and enhance readiness for audit of public financial statements.

Reform area: Fiscal and public resource management strengthened
Outcome: At least two government contracts incorporate sustainable considerations, and one procurement framework agreement put in place
Description: To support the implementation of a structured and sequenced reform agenda, promote informed decision-making in resource allocation, enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of public spending and strengthen fiscal transparency, the Cabinet approved the phased implementation of the updated PFM Road Map (2025-2030), which incorporates the relevant recommendations of the comprehensive 2025 PEFA assessment report.

Reform area: Performance, transparency and accountability of public enterprises enhanced.
Outcome: Public enterprises that adopted KPI frameworks demonstrate the achievement of at least 80% of KPIs through regular monitoring and reporting
Description: To enhance the performance and operational efficiency of the public enterprises, MFED completed the public enterprises performance review and endorsed a time bound action plan that outlines governance and institutional reforms, financial sustainability measures, capacity-building, control mechanisms and monitoring and evaluation methods.

Reform area: Performance, transparency and accountability of public enterprises enhanced.
Outcome: Public enterprises that adopted KPI frameworks demonstrate the achievement of at least 80% of KPIs through regular monitoring and reporting
Description: To further strengthen the performance of the public enterprises: (i) The Public Enterprise Monitoring Unit (PERMU), under MFED, will approve key performance indicators (KPIs) for adoption by the public enterprises to enhance accountability, transparency, and efficiency in the management and operations of SOEs; and at least two public enterprises adopt KPI frameworks. (ii) At least two public enterprises adopt gender policies to promote (a) gender-balanced recruitment processes, (b) increased representation of women in leadership and decision-making roles, (c) safe and inclusive workplace, and (d) gender-responsive operations.

Reform area: Performance, transparency and accountability of public enterprises enhanced.
Outcome: Public enterprises that adopted KPI frameworks demonstrate the achievement of at least 80% of KPIs through regular monitoring and reporting
Description: To further strengthen transparency and enhance public trust in public enterprises performance, MFED will develop and publish the first consolidated public enterprises monitoring report on MFED's website.

Reform area: Performance, transparency and accountability of public enterprises enhanced.
Outcome: Public enterprises that adopted KPI frameworks demonstrate the achievement of at least 80% of KPIs through regular monitoring and reporting
Description: To improve the transparency, accountability and financial discipline of the public enterprises and ensure the government receives critical information on the performance of the public enterprises in a timely manner, which facilitates more informed and effective decision-making: (i) MFED issued a ministerial order to establish simplified financial reporting standards for monitoring the operational performance and financials of the public entities with administrative measures for noncompliance; and (ii) at least three public enterprises submitted quarterly financial reporting (including sex-disaggregated data on staffing) in accordance with the simplified template to be published on the MFED's website.

Reform area: Fiscal management for energy transition and climate resilience advanced
Outcome: At least 50% of electricity generated from renewable energy/PV solar system nationwide (2022 baseline: 20%)
Description: To achieve cost savings by prioritizing renewable energy sources in its investment plan and reduce the country's dependence on fossil fuels, the Cabinet endorsed the Energy Bill 2025, for submission to the Parliament, which promotes the use of renewable energy sources, with the goal of achieving 100% renewable energy generation nationwide by 2030.

Reform area: Fiscal management for energy transition and climate resilience advanced
Outcome: At least 50% of electricity generated from renewable energy/PV solar system nationwide (2022 baseline: 20%)
Description: To achieve targets set in the Energy Act 2025, (i) the Cabinet will endorse policy regulation(s) to implement the Energy Act; (ii) the Tuvalu Energy Corporation will adopt Operation and Maintenance Policy to ensure the efficient, safe, and sustainable functioning of assets, infrastructure, and systems throughout their lifecycle; and (iii) government will adopt the FY2026 budget that includes renewable energy projects as part of its public investment program.

Reform area: Fiscal management for energy transition and climate resilience advanced
Outcome: At least 50% of electricity generated from renewable energy/PV solar system nationwide (2022 baseline: 20%)
Description: To ensure strategic, responsible, and targeted allocation of public funds for climate adaptation, the Cabinet endorsed the gender-responsive National Adaptation Plan (NAP) that integrates climate change adaptation into national development planning, fosters access to climate finance and strategic partnerships, and provides the financing strategy to support adaptation priorities, reducing vulnerability to climate change impacts through enhanced resilience.

Reform area: Fiscal management for energy transition and climate resilience advanced
Outcome: At least 50% of electricity generated from renewable energy/PV solar system nationwide (2022 baseline: 20%)
Description: To facilitate the implementation and achieve the targets set in the Island Strategic Plans, the government will allocate A$1 million in its FY2027 to support the planned activities.

Reform area: Fiscal management for energy transition and climate resilience advanced
Outcome: At least 50% of electricity generated from renewable energy/PV solar system nationwide (2022 baseline: 20%)
Description: To facilitate the implementation of the NAP, the Cabinet approved the National Reclamation and Relocation Strategy as a strategic framework for coastal protection, aimed at safeguarding critical infrastructure, enhancing environmental resilience, and supporting sustainable urban development, that prioritizes areas and solutions with economic and social benefits.

Reform area: Fiscal management for energy transition and climate resilience advanced
Outcome: At least 50% of electricity generated from renewable energy/PV solar system nationwide (2022 baseline: 20%)
Description: To implement cost-effective solutions nationwide enhancing fiscal resilience, the Ministry of Home Affairs, Climate Change and Environment confirmed the approvals by the relevant Chief of Islands the gender-responsive island strategic plans for four major islands—Niutao, Nui, Nukulaelae, and Funafuti—that foster the use of renewable energy technologies and climate adaptation solutions to reduce dependence on fuel based energy generation and address climate change, and support women's resilience to climate change through increased access to economic opportunities and addressing barriers.

Action 1: To achieve targets set in the Energy Act 2025, (i) the Cabinet will endorse policy regulation(s) to implement the Energy Act; (ii) the Tuvalu Energy Corporation will adopt Operation and Maintenance Policy to ensure the efficient, safe, and sustainable functioning of assets, infrastructure, and systems throughout their lifecycle; and (iii) government will adopt the FY2026 budget that includes renewable energy projects as part of its public investment program.
Action 2: To facilitate the implementation and achieve the targets set in the Island Strategic Plans, the government will allocate A$1 million in its FY2027 to support the planned activities.
Action 3: To facilitate the implementation of the NAP, the Cabinet approved the National Reclamation and Relocation Strategy as a strategic framework for coastal protection, aimed at safeguarding critical infrastructure, enhancing environmental resilience, and supporting sustainable urban development, that prioritizes areas and solutions with economic and social benefits.
Action 1: To achieve cost savings by prioritizing renewable energy sources in its investment plan and reduce the country's dependence on fossil fuels, the Cabinet endorsed the Energy Bill 2025, for submission to the Parliament, which promotes the use of renewable energy sources, with the goal of achieving 100% renewable energy generation nationwide by 2030.
